 Gen.G Come Back Against LYON to Lock In Worlds 2026 Quarterfinal Spot
 26 Oct 2026 Mark Attard 
 Photo: Dot Esports (all rights reserved) 
 Gen.G finished the Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage unbeaten after dropping Game 1 to LYON and winning the next two, Inven Global reported. The 2-1 series win sends the LCK team straight into the quarterfinals.
 Dot Esports said Gen.G are one of the first two teams through. Dplus KIA got there earlier on Day 3 with a 2-0 sweep of Movistar KOI. Both KOI and LYON now sit at 2-1 and still have a route into the knockout stage.
 Game 1 goes to LYON
 First Blood came at the nine-minute mark. Gen.G caught Dhokla's Olaf after he used his ultimate, with Kiin's Rumble getting the kill as the bot lane rotated top. LYON answered with a 4v4 mid fight that took out Chovy's Anivia and Ruler's Jhin.
 LYON then started a Baron on the 20-minute spawn and finished it without losing anyone. They used the buff to take down the mid tier 1 tower, won a mid teamfight against Alistar and Qiyana, and built up three dragons, although gold was level at 24 minutes.
 A second Baron, taken in a 5v5, and a run of teamfight wins carried them through the bottom inhibitor and on to the Nexus.
 Dot Esports described the game as skirmish-heavy, with Canyon's Qiyana ultimates repeatedly missing and Chovy struggling on Anivia.
 Gen.G level the series
 Game 2 opened with LYON taking three kills around the first dragon. Gen.G responded when Chovy used Lissandra's ultimate to stall Inspired's Vi, which gave Kiin's Ambessa time to join and secure two kills. Gen.G also killed Shen after he came to protect Saint's Akali.
 Kiin's Ambessa kept scaling, and by the 19-minute mark Gen.G had a lead of more than 5,000 gold and three dragons. LYON's Vi and Shen pairing never got going. Gen.G won a top lane teamfight at 23 minutes, then took Baron and the Dragon Soul to tie the series 1-1.
 Camille decides Game 3
 LYON had the better laning phase in the decider, putting Tristana into Chovy's Galio and pressuring Ezreal and Nautilus with Lucian and Milio. Canyon's Jayce farmed through the jungle and helped pick off Lucian and Milio in the bot lane.
 LYON still won the first dragon fight decisively. Gen.G answered by catching Tristana near the dragon and killing Maokai to take the objective. Galio fell first in the next teamfight, but Camille arrived by Teleport and drove the win, according to Inven Global.
 Gen.G took the mid inhibitor and built a three-dragon stack, then won the final fight.
 Rest of Day 3
 Dot Esports reported that Dplus KIA's Smash recorded the first pentakill of the tournament in Game 1 against Movistar KOI.
 In the other Day 3 matches, Invictus Gaming beat Hanwha Life Esports and Top Esports beat G2 Esports. Both Chinese teams lost their opening matches and are now 2-1. HLE and G2 are 1-2 and one more defeat from elimination.
